messages:
Amy K: noticing repeated latency spikes (~200-400ms increase) on long-context sessions when KV cache is under high churn. repro attached below. seems correlated with LRU eviction plus large variable-length KV entries.
Amy K: repro steps: start load test with 100 concurrent sessions, average seq len 10->512, enable kv.eviction.policy=lru, kv.cache.size=12GB. after ~30m latency spikes appear and memory RSS trends up.
Amy K: quick log snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T14:23:41Z] request_id=abc123 seq_len=480 kv_hits=0 kv_evicted=342 latency=124ms
[2026-03-15T14:23:42Z] request_id=def456 seq_len=502 kv_hits=0 kv_evicted=815 latency=520ms
[2026-03-15T14:23:43Z] request_id=ghi789 seq_len=16  kv_hits=12 kv_evicted=0   latency=18ms
```
Amy K: memory profiler (heapdiff snapshot) shows steady growth in "kv_blocks" arena and a lot of small free fragments.
Ben C: curious — do we update LRU on reads? that can cause churn if reads are frequent and we touch many items.
Carlos R: attaching pprof top:
```
134.2MB  45.0%  malloc  kv_store_alloc
43.9MB   14.7%  malloc  std::vector allocations for kv keys
22.1MB    7.4%  realloc kv_block_resize
```
Carlos R: flamegraph shows consolidation work during spikes; wall time spent in kv compaction + jemalloc fallback.
Samira V: this smells like fragmentation from variable-length values + LRU moving nodes around. jemalloc doesn't always compact small fragments. Were we using tcache?
Amy K: we run system allocator currently. I tried enabling jemalloc locally and RSS smoothed but latency still pops under eviction flurries.
Diane L: a few ideas: 1) consider not bumping LRU on reads (make it read-only access) 2) add background compaction pass when free fragmentation exceeds threshold 3) experiment with FIFO or segment-based eviction under heavy churn.
Ben C: FIFO could actually be better under producer/consumer traffic — less pointer-churn. but correctness: ensure we don't evict active prefixes used by in-flight decodes. need a quick check.
Carlos R: ran microbench: switching to FIFO reduced pointer updates by ~60% and CPU in eviction path by ~40%, but tail-latency improvement varied by workload. reproduced with a randomized session generator.
Samira V: also saw pattern where KV reuse is low because keys include session-specific salts. maybe we can normalize keys for long contexts to improve reuse.
Amy K: good call. I added a flag to coalesce session-id in keys for tokens > 256 tokens; reuse jump ~3x locally.
infra-bot: deploy queued: branch amy/kv-fifo-experiment -> staging at 2026-03-15T16:00:00Z :rocket:
Ben C: schedule: can we A/B FIFO vs LRU on staging with our long-context load? we should monitor kv_eviction_count, kv_compact_time, p95 latency.
Diane L: also add an assertion to prevent eviction of entries that are currently pinned by an active decoder (safety). we suspected some correctness edge earlier.
Carlos R: I instrumented pin_count per entry; no incorrect double-free seen but there is a race leading to brief backpressure while eviction waits for pins to release. that's what causes the latency spike.
Samira V: patch idea: make eviction non-blocking by moving evicted entries to a pending-free queue handled by background worker that waits on pins. eviction path returns immediately.
Amy K: sounds promising. I'm going to: create a micro-repro test, enable FIFO on staging, add pending-free queue, and run 6h soak. I'll post results.
Ben C: if FIFO + pending-free queue + key normalization reduces p95 by >20% and keeps RSS stable, we can consider it default for 0.14 rollout.
Diane L: filing follow-ups: 1) perf-PR for FIFO toggle + metrics 2) compaction microbenchmark 3) allocator experiment with jemalloc config. assign owners?
Amy K: I'll own PR + staging run. Carlos will do compaction bench. Samira will try allocator configs and key-normalization perf.
Amy K: thanks all, will update thread with soak logs and flamegraphs. :thumbsup:
additional_notes: Repro and traces referenced; thread focuses on eviction policy interaction with allocator and pinned-entry correctness.
